modalLead: A big one. Typing on the dashboard finally does only what you meant, the inbox counts what you can actually see, and the monitors say why something failed instead of leaving a blank.

items.text: What you type arrives whole. Typing github used to open a bookmark halfway through and leave hub behind, and a word starting with g lost its first letter. Nothing opens by itself any more: the list narrows as you type and Enter opens the top result. A bookmark shortcut is one keystroke longer — type it, press Enter — and it behaves the same tomorrow as today.
j and k move the cursor again. They picked a row and then typed the letter over it, so the selection vanished in the same keypress. They move once a row is selected; the arrows are how you get there.

The line you type into says what it is. The key that starts each mode sits in front of it — > search, : commands, ? finders — and once there is something typed, an × clears it. Escape clears it on screen too, instead of leaving the old text behind.

A short key legend under the bookmarks, for anyone who wants one. It appears only once you start moving with the keyboard and goes again when you open something. Switch it on or off under Behavior → General.
Shortcut hints on the toolbar icons are now off. They were on for everyone since they existed; the switch is in the same place if you want them back.

Every number counts the links you can see. A search or a site filter now narrows the tiles, the pills and the badge along with the list, Mark all read becomes Mark shown read while something is narrowing the view, and the first tile is called Active — a sleeping link is deliberately not part of it.

Sleeping links are no longer invisible. A line under the list says how many are asleep and when the first one wakes, and takes you to them. The site picker no longer offers a site whose only link is asleep and then answers with "no matching links".

Import a list back in. The inbox could always be exported and never read back. Import sits beside CSV and JSON, skips links that are already there, and says afterwards how many arrived, how many were already in and how many did not fit.
A link can go back to unread, and the page description is shown under the title. Marking something read by mistake used to leave deleting as the only way out.
A failure says why. DNS, timeout, refused, TLS, content — it is on the outage and in the export, where the reason used to be blank for anything that was not an HTTP error.
One dropped check no longer counts as an outage. A failed check is tried once more, five seconds later, and only recorded if it fails again. A single hiccup used to dent your uptime for a month.
Certificate warnings reach everyone. They came only from bookmarks set to Monitor, so an install using the ordinary periodic checks never saw one. Every check contributes now.
A 30-day figure that only has a week behind it says so, rather than printing a month either way.

A recovery says how long it was down — "back online after 3h 12m" — you can mute or unmute a whole selection at once, the trend chart can draw broken, stale, unchecked and score instead of only healthy, and the three-second limit on a check is now a setting for services that legitimately take longer.

Search can say "not". A minus in front of any filter excludes instead of selects — tag:dev -status:pinned is "dev links I have not pinned". And status:untagged and status:noted finally answer the two questions the bar could not ask.
:trash opens the recycle bin from the dashboard, where deleted bookmarks, pages and categories wait 30 days. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter on a result opens it in a new tab, whatever your setting says.

Moving a bookmark can be undone. Deleting one has offered Undo for a long time; moving one — or twenty at once — offered nothing, and each bookmark now goes back to the category it actually came from.

A category can carry an icon and be moved with the keyboard. Right-click its header for Icon…, type an emoji and watch the heading follow along; Alt with the left or right arrow moves the category itself.

Settings that are a shape are drawn. Columns, density, spacing, margins and type size show a small picture of what they do, and it redraws as you change them. Help does the same where the subject is a layout.
A setting changed on one device arrives on the other. The second screen used to keep its old look until you reloaded it by hand.
A failed automatic backup says so. The tile turns red and names the error — a full disk could stop backups for months while the panel looked perfectly normal.
A bookmark row in config says where it lives as one crumb, page then category, and each half filters the list. A fresh install now starts on Retro CRT; your theme is untouched.
